finding.claim: Unvalidated server-side fetch: GET /rss passes the raw u query parameter to URI.open, letting an unauthenticated caller make the server request arbitrary http/https/ftp URLs, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned, so the SSRF is readable.
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read (app.rb:8); response prefix returned at app.rb:9

trace.note: get "/rss" route accepts attacker-controlled query parameter u
params[:u] passed directly to URI.open with no transform or check
open-uri issues the outbound request and follows http<->https redirects by default
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched body to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allow-list; no host allow-list (TRUSTED at app.rb:5 is only used by /trusted); no private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking; no DNS pinning; no redirect control; no port restriction. Note: URI.open falls back to Kernel.open for scheme-less strings, which is a separate local file read issue on the same line. Checked and not reported: /trusted (app.rb:12-15) validates the same parsed URI object it fetches, with no redirects followed and only trusted hosts permitted; /version (app.rb:18-20) uses a constant URL.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7-10 has no scheme, host, IP, or redirect check between params[:u] and URI.open at app.rb:8. The only allow-list, TRUSTED at app.rb:5, is used solely by /trusted at app.rb:14, not /rss. app.rb:9 returns data[0, 400] to the caller.
verdict.reason: The route at app.rb:7 takes params[:u] with no authentication and passes it unchecked to URI.open at app.rb:8, whose open-uri follows redirects by default; app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes of the response, so the SSRF is readable as claimed. The candidate's trace lines all match the file.
